prompt: A production Kubernetes cluster is running at 87% memory across all nodes. A critical security patch requires rolling restarts, but each restart temporarily spikes memory to 110% of the pod's request. Decide how to sequence the rollout so the patch lands today without triggering OOM kills on customer-facing services.
rubric_items: sequence restarts to stay below 100% memory at each node
temporarily reduce pod replicas before restarting high-memory pods
prioritize non-customer-facing services in the restart sequence
define per-node memory budget that absorbs the 110% spike
specify rollback trigger if OOM events begin occurring

prompt: Two engineering teams independently built caching layers for the same backend service. Merging them would save infrastructure cost but risks a multi-week integration that blocks both teams' roadmaps. Decide whether to merge now, later, or never, and what information you need to commit to one path.
rubric_items: define criteria for merge versus defer versus abandon
quantify integration cost against infrastructure savings
identify ownership and interface boundary for each caching layer
specify information needed to commit to one path
propose a phased or pilot merge to reduce risk

prompt: A startup has runway for 14 months but a competitor just raised a large round. The CEO wants to accelerate hiring, but the CTO argues that onboarding slows the existing team. Design a hiring plan that addresses both speed and velocity preservation.
rubric_items: balance hiring pace against onboarding velocity drag
prioritize roles that unblock existing team bottlenecks
preserve at least 12 months of effective runway
account for onboarding ramp time in productivity projections
set a checkpoint to reassess if competitive pressure changes

prompt: A compliance audit revealed that 11% of production data lacks proper consent records. The legal team wants an immediate freeze on all data processing, but the product team says a freeze would breach SLAs with three enterprise clients. Propose a plan that satisfies both constraints.
rubric_items: propose a partial freeze covering only non-consented data
identify which processing activities remain legally safe to continue
communicate proactively with enterprise clients about affected SLAs
set a deadline for remediating missing consent records
establish a legal review gate before resuming full processing

prompt: A model fine-tuned on synthetic data performs well on the synthetic validation set but poorly on real user queries. You have budget for either collecting 500 real labeled examples or running a domain-adaptation technique that requires no new labels. Decide which path to take and what early signal would cause you to switch.
rubric_items: compare expected accuracy lift from both approaches on real queries
define early signal indicators within the first week
specify switch criteria if the chosen path underperforms
account for data collection time in the total timeline estimate
validate improvement on held-out real user queries

prompt: A database migration from PostgreSQL to a distributed NewSQL system is 60% complete. The remaining tables have complex foreign-key constraints that the new system handles differently. Continuing risks subtle data integrity bugs; rolling back wastes three months of work. Lay out criteria for the go/no-go decision.
rubric_items: enumerate specific foreign-key integrity tests for remaining tables
define rollback cost and feasibility at current completion state
set measurable criteria distinguishing acceptable from unacceptable integrity risk
propose a canary cutover to detect silent data corruption
identify which remaining tables can migrate safely first

prompt: An on-call engineer discovers that a rate limiter is silently dropping 2% of legitimate API requests during peak hours. Raising the limit risks exposing the service to abuse; keeping it risks losing paying customers. Propose a same-day mitigation and a longer-term fix.
rubric_items: implement same-day mitigation without opening the service to abuse
distinguish legitimate traffic from abusive traffic at the limiter
quantify customer impact from the current 2% drop rate
propose a longer-term fix with measurable success criteria
include monitoring to detect abuse increase after mitigation

prompt: A research team wants to submit a paper in 10 days, but the key ablation study requires a GPU cluster that is fully booked for 7 days. They can either run a smaller ablation on available hardware or negotiate for cluster time by delaying another team's work. Plan the path that maximizes paper strength without burning political capital.
rubric_items: design a smaller ablation runnable on available hardware within the deadline
assess whether the reduced ablation supports the main claim
evaluate political cost of displacing another team's cluster time
identify which ablation experiments are strictly necessary versus optional
set a decision point before the 7-day cluster wait ends

prompt: A SaaS product's free tier is consuming 40% of infrastructure costs but drives 60% of paid conversions. Finance wants to cut the free tier; growth wants to expand it. Design an experiment that resolves the disagreement with data within 30 days.
rubric_items: design a controlled experiment isolating free-tier impact on paid conversion
define primary metric and guardrail metrics for the 30-day window
estimate minimum detectable effect given available conversion volume
include a holdout group to measure counterfactual conversion
specify an early-stop rule if churn accelerates

prompt: A CI pipeline takes 47 minutes. Developers are batching commits to avoid waiting, which increases merge conflict rates. You can either parallelize the test suite (engineering cost) or split the monorepo (organizational cost). Decide which to pursue first and what metrics would validate the choice.
rubric_items: compare engineering and organizational cost for both options
identify which slow tests are most parallelizable without ordering issues
define CI latency metrics to validate improvement after implementation
estimate merge-conflict rate reduction from faster pipeline feedback
propose an interim measure to reduce commit batching immediately

prompt: A deployed fraud detection model has a 0.3% false positive rate, but each false positive locks a legitimate customer's account for 24 hours. Lowering the threshold reduces false positives but lets more fraud through. Design a decision framework that accounts for both customer trust and financial loss.
rubric_items: define separate decision thresholds for different customer risk tiers
quantify false-positive account-lock cost against fraud loss prevented
propose an expedited review or appeals path for locked accounts
track false-positive rate and fraud-pass-through rate as dual KPIs
set a maximum account-lock duration to bound customer harm

prompt: A microservices architecture has 14 services, but observability shows that 80% of latency comes from a chain of 4 synchronous calls. Refactoring to async would fix latency but breaks the exactly-once delivery guarantee that finance depends on. Plan a migration that preserves the guarantee while reducing tail latency.
rubric_items: identify the async delivery pattern that preserves exactly-once semantics
propose incremental migration starting with lowest-risk service call chains
preserve synchronous fallback for finance-critical calls during migration
measure tail latency improvement at each migration step
define rollback criteria if exactly-once guarantee cannot be validated

prompt: A team discovers that their A/B test has been running with a logging bug that drops 15% of events non-randomly — mobile users on slow connections are underrepresented. The test has been running for 3 weeks. Decide whether the results are salvageable and what analysis would confirm it.
rubric_items: test for differential dropout rates between control and treatment arms
quantify bias magnitude if mobile users are reweighted or imputed
propose reweighted analysis using inverse propensity or post-stratification
assess whether treatment effect estimates change after bias correction
state the bias bound if results are deemed salvageable

prompt: A critical third-party API provider announces a 4x price increase effective in 60 days. Building an in-house replacement would take 90 days. Switching to a cheaper alternative would take 30 days but has fewer features. Plan a transition that avoids both service disruption and overspending.
rubric_items: use the first 30 days to pilot the cheaper alternative
negotiate a temporary extension or grandfather clause with the current provider
identify which missing alternative features are genuine blockers
set a day-30 decision point to commit to one path
budget for a cost-overlap period while running both solutions

prompt: An ML pipeline retrains nightly, but model drift detection fires 3-4 false alarms per week, causing alert fatigue. The team is considering raising the drift threshold, but the last real drift event was caught at the current threshold. Decide how to reduce false alarms without missing genuine drift.
rubric_items: separate feature drift from label drift before adjusting threshold
add a secondary confirmation step before triggering full alerts
track false-alarm rate and missed-drift rate as dual objectives
backtest any threshold change against the last confirmed drift event
implement alert-fatigue mitigation without increasing missed-detection risk

prompt: A company's SOC 2 audit is in 6 weeks, but the engineering team just discovered that their secrets rotation policy has not been enforced for 8 months. Rotating all secrets at once risks outages; doing nothing risks audit failure. Plan the rotation sequence.
rubric_items: prioritize rotation of externally exposed secrets first
schedule rotations during low-traffic windows to minimize outage risk
validate each rotated secret in staging before production cutover
document rotation evidence for audit trail before the 6-week deadline
define a rollback procedure for each secret rotation

prompt: A product manager wants to ship a feature that uses user browsing history to personalize recommendations. The legal team flags GDPR concerns, and the privacy engineer says the anonymization pipeline is not yet production-ready. The feature is expected to increase engagement by 12%. Decide what to ship and when.
rubric_items: ship only on data where valid user consent already exists
specify minimum anonymization requirements needed for a compliant launch
define a phased rollout deferring browsing-history signal until pipeline is ready
quantify engagement lift achievable with the consent-compliant data subset
require legal sign-off before browsing data enters the recommendation model

prompt: Two data centers serve traffic in active-active mode. One data center's cooling system is degrading, and the facility team estimates failure within 72 hours. Failing over all traffic to the other data center would exceed its capacity by 20% during peak hours. Plan the response.
rubric_items: begin gradual traffic shift before cooling failure not after
identify which services to deprioritize during the 20% over-capacity period
coordinate with facility team on precise cooling failure timeline
pre-scale receiving data center before initiating full failover
define rollback and restoration plan once cooling is repaired

prompt: A machine learning team is training a large model and discovers that 5% of the training data contains near-duplicate entries from the evaluation set. Removing them and retraining costs $40K in compute. Keeping them invalidates all published benchmarks. Decide the path forward.
rubric_items: quantify benchmark score inflation from near-duplicate eval contamination
determine which benchmarks are invalidated versus still valid
compare retraining cost against reputational risk of contaminated results
add deduplication check as a standard pipeline gate going forward
disclose contamination transparently in any publication or public benchmark

prompt: An open-source library your product depends on just had its maintainer mass-delete all releases from the package registry in a protest action. Your CI/CD is broken, and your local cache has the last three versions. Plan immediate recovery and long-term resilience.
rubric_items: pin CI/CD to cached local versions immediately to restore builds
verify compatibility and safety of cached versions before promoting
identify alternate mirrors or registries that still host the releases
evaluate forking under a vendor namespace for long-term control
implement lockfile pinning or vendoring to prevent recurrence

prompt: A feature flag system shows that a gradually rolled-out feature is causing a 7% increase in error rates for the 5% of users who have it enabled. But those same users show 15% higher retention. Decide whether to continue the rollout, pause, or roll back, and what additional data would change your decision.
rubric_items: identify which error types account for the 7% increase
assess whether errors are user-visible or backend-only
define a maximum tolerable error threshold before automatic rollback
confirm retention lift is causal not correlational via cohort analysis
specify additional data that would distinguish acceptable from critical regression

prompt: A team of 8 engineers is split across 3 time zones. A critical production incident requires coordinated debugging, but it is midnight for 3 of the engineers and early morning for 2 others. Design an incident response protocol that is effective without burning out the team.
rubric_items: assign incident commander from the timezone with most availability
use asynchronous status updates to avoid requiring synchronous attendance
define a clear handoff protocol between timezone shifts
protect engineers in the midnight timezone unless their expertise is critical
set a severity threshold for waking off-hours engineers

prompt: A government contract requires all data to remain within national borders, but the best-performing cloud region for latency is in a neighboring country. The compliant region has 3x the latency and 2x the cost. Plan an architecture that meets the legal requirement without destroying user experience.
rubric_items: use in-country edge caching to reduce last-mile latency
identify latency-sensitive workloads needing special architectural treatment
quantify user experience impact of 3x latency with real measurements
document compliance boundary clearly for regulatory review
evaluate in-country CDN or POP node to narrow the latency gap

prompt: A startup's runway is 8 months. The CTO proposes rewriting the backend in Rust for performance gains, estimating 4 months of work. The CEO argues the current Python backend is fast enough and engineering time should go to features. Decide how to arbitrate this with evidence rather than opinion.
rubric_items: profile Python backend to identify actual performance bottlenecks
define performance thresholds that would justify a full rewrite
estimate feature delivery opportunity cost during the 4-month Rust rewrite
propose a targeted Rust module for the single hottest path as a pilot
calculate break-even point where performance gains justify rewrite cost within runway

prompt: An internal tool used by 200 employees has a known SQL injection vulnerability. Patching it requires refactoring the ORM layer, which will take 2 weeks. A WAF rule could block the attack vector immediately but would also block some legitimate queries. Decide the sequencing.
rubric_items: deploy WAF rule immediately to block the sql injection attack vector
enumerate which legitimate queries the WAF rule would disrupt
schedule ORM refactoring to begin under WAF protection window
define a rollback criterion if WAF causes unacceptable query failures
treat WAF as temporary mitigation not a permanent fix

prompt: A recommendation system's click-through rate improved 8% after a change, but downstream purchase conversion dropped 3%. The product team celebrates the CTR win while the revenue team raises alarms. Design an analysis plan that identifies which metric should drive the decision.
rubric_items: establish revenue impact as the primary decision metric over CTR
test whether click-bait content explains the CTR-conversion divergence
run a holdback experiment isolating the recommendation change
check whether CTR and conversion changes affect the same user cohort
define a blended metric that weights clicks and purchases appropriately

prompt: A data warehouse query that generates the CEO's daily dashboard has grown from 2 minutes to 45 minutes over 6 months due to data volume growth. The options are: optimize the query, pre-aggregate data nightly, move to a columnar store, or reduce the dashboard scope. Decide the approach given a 1-week deadline.
rubric_items: profile the query to identify the dominant performance bottleneck
implement pre-aggregated nightly summaries as the fastest available fix
scope the dashboard to remove the least-used high-cost queries
defer columnar store migration given the one-week deadline constraint
measure query execution plan after each optimization step before proceeding

prompt: An intern accidentally pushed AWS credentials to a public GitHub repository 4 hours ago. The credentials have been used to spin up crypto-mining instances in 3 regions. Plan the incident response covering immediate containment, forensics, cost mitigation, and process changes.
rubric_items: revoke all exposed credentials and rotate secrets within minutes
terminate all unauthorized crypto-mining instances across all three regions
audit CloudTrail logs to determine the full scope of unauthorized access
estimate and dispute the fraudulent compute charges with AWS
implement pre-commit secret scanning to prevent future credential leaks

prompt: A clinical trial data pipeline must produce results for a regulatory submission in 48 hours. A statistician discovers that one site's data has systematic measurement bias. Including it may bias results; excluding it reduces statistical power below the pre-registered threshold. Decide the analytical strategy.
rubric_items: quantify the measurement bias magnitude and direction at the affected site
assess whether site exclusion drops statistical power below the pre-registered threshold
consult the statistical analysis plan for pre-specified handling of site anomalies
document the exclusion rationale to satisfy regulatory reviewers
propose a sensitivity analysis including and excluding the biased site

prompt: A mobile app update reduced crash rates by 40% but increased battery drain by 25%. App store reviews are improving due to stability, but power users are complaining about battery life. Decide whether to release a hotfix, revert, or ship as-is with a settings toggle.
rubric_items: profile the code change to identify the specific source of battery drain
segment battery drain impact by device tier and usage pattern
compare crash rate improvement value against battery complaint and uninstall rate
implement a settings toggle to let users choose stability over battery life
define a rollback threshold based on app store rating or power-user churn

prompt: A team maintaining a monolith wants to extract a payments microservice. The monolith has 340 direct database queries against the payments tables from 12 different modules. Propose a strangler-fig migration plan that avoids a feature freeze and maintains transaction consistency.
rubric_items: map all 340 database queries against payments tables by owning module
introduce a payments service interface layer without changing existing query behavior
migrate modules to the service one at a time behind feature flags
maintain distributed transaction consistency during the dual-write phase
define per-module acceptance criteria before cutting off direct database access

prompt: A machine learning model serves real-time predictions with a p99 latency of 50ms. A new regulation requires all predictions to include an explanation. The cheapest explanation method adds 200ms of latency. Decide how to comply without breaking latency SLAs.
rubric_items: pre-compute explanations asynchronously and attach them to stored prediction records
explore lightweight approximation methods that stay within the latency SLA
cache explanations for repeated input patterns to reduce per-request overhead
negotiate a tiered SLA that separately bounds explanation delivery latency
validate that explanation approximations satisfy the regulatory definition of explainability

prompt: A hedge fund's backtesting framework shows a strategy with 18% annual returns, but live paper-trading shows only 4%. The quant team suspects slippage modeling is wrong, but fixing it might invalidate 6 months of research. Plan the investigation and decide when to stop the live test.
rubric_items: identify whether slippage model differences account for the full 14pp live gap
compare execution timestamps in paper-trading against backtest timing assumptions
run a corrected backtest with realistic slippage before abandoning the strategy
define a stop-loss threshold for the live paper-trading test
separate slippage from market impact and signal decay as distinct gap sources

prompt: A DevOps team manages 300 servers with Ansible playbooks that have grown organically over 3 years. No one fully understands the dependency graph, and a recent change broke 40 servers. The team can either freeze changes and audit, or continue shipping with extra manual testing. Decide the approach.
rubric_items: freeze all non-critical playbook changes and restore the 40 broken servers first
document the playbook execution order and module interdependencies
introduce a staging environment to test playbooks before future production runs
identify the change that caused the breakage using diff and execution logs
define a minimum viable playbook set and mark the rest for deprecation

prompt: A SaaS company discovers that their largest customer, responsible for 30% of revenue, is using the product in a way that violates the Terms of Service and may expose the company to legal liability. Cutting them off immediately threatens the company's financial health. Plan the response.
rubric_items: obtain a legal opinion on the company's liability exposure before taking action
notify the customer privately of the ToS violation before any enforcement step
negotiate a remediation timeline that removes legal exposure without losing the account
document the violation and company response for the legal record
model the financial runway impact of losing 30% revenue in the worst-case scenario

prompt: A real-time bidding system processes 500K requests per second. A new privacy regulation requires checking each request against a consent database before bidding. The consent database can handle 100K reads per second. Design a system that complies without dropping 80% of bid opportunities.
rubric_items: implement a local consent cache with a short TTL to reduce database reads
pre-fetch consent records by user ID before the bidding window opens
define a fail-open vs fail-closed policy for consent cache misses
use probabilistic data structures to filter clearly non-consenting users cheaply
measure cache hit rate to quantify bid opportunities preserved vs dropped

prompt: A research team has two promising approaches for a conference deadline in 3 weeks. Approach A has stronger theoretical backing but only preliminary results. Approach B has solid empirical results but a weaker story. There is only enough compute and writing bandwidth for one paper. Decide which to pursue.
rubric_items: assess whether approach A's theoretical backing can substitute for missing empirical results
evaluate which approach addresses the more impactful or timely research question
check whether approach B's empirical results meet the venue's acceptance bar
estimate remaining compute and writing bandwidth for each approach realistically
set a hard decision date to commit before deadline pressure forces a poor choice

prompt: A deployment accidentally wrote production data to a staging database for 6 hours. Both databases now have divergent records. The staging database has already been used by QA to validate the next release. Plan data reconciliation without blocking either the production fix or the upcoming release.
rubric_items: identify all records written to staging that conflict with canonical production records
snapshot the staging database before reconciliation to preserve QA test context
restore production data integrity without overwriting the staging QA state
replay the divergent staging writes against production to merge any missing records
provide QA a clean validated staging environment that unblocks the release validation

prompt: An autonomous vehicle fleet operator discovers that the perception model performs 15% worse in rain but the safety certification was based on dry-weather testing. Pulling the fleet off the road costs $2M per week in lost revenue. Continuing operation in rain risks an incident. Decide on operational constraints and a testing plan.
rubric_items: immediately restrict fleet operation in rainfall above a defined intensity threshold
notify the safety certification authority of the discovered rain-condition performance gap
design a targeted wet-weather test suite using historical sensor data from the fleet
quantify expected incident probability cost against the $2M weekly revenue opportunity
define measurable performance thresholds that must be met before lifting rain restrictions

prompt: A team lead has two senior engineers who disagree fundamentally about the system architecture. One wants event sourcing; the other wants traditional CRUD with change-data-capture. The disagreement is blocking a key project. Design a technical decision process that resolves this within one week without alienating either engineer.
rubric_items: define the specific technical requirements the architecture must satisfy before the PoC
assign a time-boxed proof-of-concept to each approach using a shared representative test case
establish objective decision criteria agreed upon before either PoC begins
involve a neutral technical arbiter to evaluate results without bias
document the final decision rationale to prevent relitigating the debate later

prompt: A financial services company must migrate from an end-of-life mainframe to cloud infrastructure. The mainframe runs COBOL batch jobs that produce regulatory reports due monthly. The next report is due in 18 days. Plan the migration so the regulatory deadline is met even if the cloud system is not fully ready.
rubric_items: run the COBOL batch jobs on the mainframe to produce the current regulatory report
run the cloud system in parallel against the mainframe to validate output parity
identify which report outputs can be produced manually if the cloud system fails
define a go/no-go checkpoint for cloud migration well before the 18-day deadline
preserve a mainframe rollback path available through the regulatory submission date

prompt: A content moderation AI flags 5% of legitimate posts as violations, causing user complaints. Reducing sensitivity lets harmful content through. The platform is under regulatory scrutiny for both over-moderation and under-moderation simultaneously. Design a system that addresses both failure modes.
rubric_items: segment flagged content by violation type to calibrate sensitivity thresholds independently
introduce a human review queue for borderline cases to reduce false-positive rate
use separate confidence thresholds for high-severity versus low-severity violation categories
track over-moderation and under-moderation rates as separate reported metrics
establish an appeals process that generates labeled data for model retraining

prompt: A distributed team uses 5 different observability tools due to historical acquisitions. The monthly cost is $180K combined. Consolidating to one tool would save $120K/year but requires 3 months of migration during which monitoring coverage will have gaps. Decide the migration strategy.
rubric_items: audit which tool covers which service and identify overlap versus unique coverage
migrate lowest-risk services first to validate the consolidated tool before critical services
maintain parallel coverage for critical services throughout the migration window
define monitoring coverage thresholds below which migration is paused
quantify the $120K annual savings against the cost of an incident during coverage gaps

prompt: A chip design team discovers a timing violation in their ASIC 2 weeks before tape-out. The fix requires re-routing a critical path, which could take 1-4 weeks depending on complexity. Delaying tape-out costs $500K per week. Shipping with the violation risks a respin costing $2M. Decide the path.
rubric_items: characterize the timing violation to determine worst-case functional failure probability
start re-routing the critical path while assessing risk in parallel to save time
define a hard decision date to commit to delay before $500K per week costs compound
evaluate whether a conservative timing guard band can mask the violation acceptably
compare the $2M respin cost against the expected cost of shipping the violation

prompt: An e-commerce platform's search relevance team improved their ranking model, but the improved model surfaces more long-tail products. This increases search quality metrics but decreases ad revenue because long-tail products have lower ad bids. Plan how to resolve the conflict between search quality and ad revenue.
rubric_items: measure ad revenue loss attributable specifically to long-tail product surfacing
separate the effect of the ranking model from advertiser bid distribution on long-tail items
test whether improving ad quality scores for long-tail products recovers lost revenue
define a blended objective function that maintains search quality with a revenue floor
run holdback experiments to isolate the ranking change's causal revenue impact

prompt: A hospital's EHR system needs a security patch, but applying it requires 4 hours of downtime. The hospital cannot go offline for 4 hours without patient safety risk. The patch fixes a vulnerability that has a known exploit in the wild. Decide the maintenance window strategy.
rubric_items: identify the lowest-risk maintenance window with minimum active patient procedures
prepare manual fallback workflows for all critical clinical functions during downtime
coordinate with clinical staff to reschedule elective procedures around the patch window
stage the patch on a non-production EHR environment first to validate the procedure
notify all departments with a specific downtime start time and recovery protocol

prompt: A video game studio is 3 months from launch and discovers that their netcode has a desync bug that occurs in 1-in-500 matches. Fixing it requires rewriting the state reconciliation layer. Shipping with the bug will result in bad reviews. Delaying launch costs $1.5M per month. Plan the response.
rubric_items: characterize the desync reproduction conditions before committing to a full rewrite
attempt a targeted fix of the state reconciliation trigger as the first option
estimate the rewrite timeline with confidence intervals not a single point estimate
define a launch-blocking desync frequency threshold based on expected review impact
plan a post-launch patch track if the bug rate falls below the blocking threshold

prompt: A company's SSO provider had a security breach. All employee sessions must be invalidated, but doing so during business hours would lock out 2,000 employees simultaneously, including the support team handling a major customer escalation. Plan the session rotation.
rubric_items: exempt the active support team sessions from the initial invalidation wave
stagger session invalidation by team priority to avoid a simultaneous company-wide lockout
pre-position re-authentication instructions to all employees before invalidation begins
resolve the active customer escalation before invalidating the support team sessions
confirm all compromised sessions are invalidated within a defined maximum time window

prompt: A climate research team's simulation uses a legacy Fortran solver that is the only implementation of their novel equations. The solver runs on hardware being decommissioned in 6 months. Porting to modern hardware requires either rewriting in C++ or using an automatic transpiler with known accuracy issues. Plan the transition.
rubric_items: assess transpiler accuracy loss against the C++ rewrite timeline
validate numerical equivalence between old and new implementations
document the novel equations independently of the Fortran codebase
plan a parallel validation run before decommissioning the legacy hardware
define a fallback if the rewrite overruns the 6-month hardware deadline

prompt: A logistics company's route optimization algorithm minimizes fuel cost, but drivers complain that the routes are unpredictable and stressful. Driver turnover has increased 20% since deploying the algorithm. Decide how to balance algorithmic efficiency against driver satisfaction without reverting to manual routing.
rubric_items: quantify driver turnover cost against fuel savings from the optimizer
identify which route characteristics cause the most driver stress
introduce predictability or consistency constraints into the route optimizer
pilot route changes with driver feedback before full deployment
avoid reverting to manual routing while addressing satisfaction issues

prompt: A team discovers that their feature store has been serving stale features for 12% of predictions over the past month due to a cache invalidation bug. All model performance metrics during this period are suspect. Decide how to assess the true impact and whether affected models need retraining.
rubric_items: identify which models received stale features and for how long
estimate the staleness magnitude and affected prediction windows
compare model performance metrics during stale versus clean periods
define a staleness impact threshold that triggers mandatory retraining
fix the cache invalidation bug before initiating any retraining

prompt: A supply chain platform must onboard a new supplier whose data format is incompatible with the existing schema. Building a custom adapter takes 4 weeks, but the supplier's products are needed in 2 weeks for a seasonal demand spike. The supplier cannot change their format. Plan a solution that meets the timeline.
rubric_items: design a lightweight data bridge that meets the 2-week seasonal deadline
develop the permanent adapter in parallel with the interim bridge
validate data fidelity of the interim bridge against the target schema
plan a cutover from the interim bridge to the permanent adapter post-season
define error handling for supplier format edge cases during the interim period

prompt: A quantum computing startup's error correction code works in simulation but fails on real hardware due to crosstalk between qubits. They have access to the hardware for only 8 hours per week. Design an experimental plan that maximizes diagnostic information per hardware session.
rubric_items: design experiments that distinguish crosstalk sources within each 8-hour session
use qubit pair isolation tests to map the crosstalk topology
pre-screen protocol candidates in simulation before spending hardware time
analyze hardware results between sessions to refine next-session hypotheses
define a minimum characterization goal for each hardware session

prompt: A platform team wants to deprecate an internal API that 45 services depend on. The replacement API is ready but has different semantics for error handling. Forcing migration risks breaking services; allowing indefinite dual-maintenance wastes engineering resources. Plan a deprecation timeline.
rubric_items: categorize the 45 dependent services by migration complexity and criticality
document the error handling semantic differences between old and new API
phase the deprecation timeline with defined service migration milestones
provide compatibility shims or migration tooling to lower adoption friction
enforce a hard sunset date to end dual-maintenance overhead

prompt: A cybersecurity team detects an active intrusion in a network segment that hosts both production servers and a honeypot. Isolating the segment stops the attacker but also takes down production. Leaving it open allows intelligence gathering but risks lateral movement. Decide the containment strategy.
rubric_items: assess lateral movement risk before choosing observation over containment
define a time-bounded intelligence gathering window with clear trip wires
isolate honeypot traffic from production servers if partial segmentation is possible
prepare a production failover path before pulling the full isolation trigger
coordinate with the incident response team before any containment decision

prompt: A pharmaceutical company's drug discovery pipeline found a compound that shows efficacy in two indications. Pursuing both in parallel doubles the clinical trial budget. Choosing one risks missing the larger market. The patent clock is ticking. Design the portfolio decision framework.
rubric_items: estimate market size and unmet need for each clinical indication
assess which indication has the faster regulatory approval pathway
evaluate co-development or partnership options to share clinical trial costs
define criteria for dropping one indication if the budget must be reduced
align the portfolio decision timeline with the patent expiry window to preserve exclusivity

prompt: A media streaming service notices that their CDN costs spike 3x during live events, but pre-purchasing reserved capacity for peak would waste 70% of it during normal hours. Design a capacity strategy that handles spikes without chronic over-provisioning.
rubric_items: model the cost crossover between on-demand surge pricing and reserved capacity
identify the predictability window for live events to enable pre-scaling
design tiered caching to offload origin traffic during peak live events
negotiate burst or spot capacity contracts for event-driven spike coverage
set auto-scaling triggers calibrated to live event start signals

prompt: A robotics team's SLAM algorithm works indoors but fails outdoors due to GPS drift and visual feature sparsity. A conference demo is in 2 weeks, and the venue is outdoor. They can either constrain the demo to a small well-mapped area or attempt a sensor fusion fix. Decide the approach and fallback plan.
rubric_items: assess whether a well-mapped constrained area reliably eliminates outdoor SLAM failures
scope the sensor fusion fix to the most impactful improvement achievable in 2 weeks
define clear fallback trigger conditions before the demo day
rehearse the demo route in the exact venue conditions beforehand
prepare a credible narrative for a constrained demo if full outdoor SLAM is not ready

prompt: A fintech company's KYC verification rejects 30% of legitimate applicants from developing countries because their ID documents don't match the template database. Adding more templates requires 3 months of data collection. The company is losing market share to competitors who accept more document types. Plan an interim solution.
rubric_items: implement a manual review queue for legitimate applicants rejected by template mismatch
prioritize the highest-volume unsupported document types for accelerated template addition
apply risk-based tiering to allow lower-risk applicants with non-template documents
partner with a third-party ID verification provider as an interim bridge
track false rejection rate by country to measure interim solution effectiveness

prompt: A CI system uses flaky end-to-end tests that fail 8% of the time due to timing issues. Developers re-run failed pipelines routinely, costing 15% of CI compute. Removing the flaky tests risks missing real bugs. Fixing each test individually would take months. Propose a systematic approach.
rubric_items: rank flaky tests by failure frequency to prioritize the highest-cost offenders
quarantine known flaky tests without removing them from the test suite
implement automatic retry with failure logging to separate flakes from real bugs
assign ownership and remediation deadlines to all quarantined flaky tests
define a pass rate threshold below which a test is quarantined versus immediately removed

prompt: An ML team discovers that their dataset has a label bias: annotators from one region systematically rate sentiment more positively than another region. The model has already been deployed for 2 months. Decide how to quantify the impact on production predictions and whether a recall of past results is necessary.
rubric_items: quantify the sentiment score divergence between regional annotator groups
measure production prediction distribution shift by region since deployment
define a bias impact threshold that triggers a recall or correction of past predictions
retrain with bias-corrected annotations before any re-deployment
implement regional stratification in all future annotation pipelines

prompt: A renewable energy grid operator needs to balance supply from intermittent solar and wind sources with demand that peaks at sunset when solar drops. Battery storage covers 60% of the gap, but a heatwave is forecast that will push demand 25% above normal. Plan the energy dispatch strategy for the next 72 hours.
rubric_items: project hourly supply-demand gap across the full 72-hour heatwave window
schedule battery discharge to prioritize the highest-deficit sunset periods
activate demand response programs to reduce peak load before battery depletion
coordinate with grid interconnects or emergency reserves for the residual shortfall
define load-shedding thresholds and customer priority tiers if all reserves are exhausted

prompt: A software vendor's on-premise customers are 4 major versions behind the current release. Supporting old versions consumes 35% of engineering capacity. Forcing upgrades risks losing customers to competitors who support longer. Decide a version support policy that balances engineering efficiency with customer retention.
rubric_items: classify customers by current version and contractual support obligations
define a minimum supported version policy with a published sunset schedule
offer migration incentives or an assisted upgrade path to accelerate customer adoption
quantify per-version engineering cost to justify each end-of-life decision
identify customers where churn risk justifies negotiated extended support exceptions

prompt: A trading firm's risk engine calculates Value-at-Risk in a batch process that finishes at 7 AM. Regulatory reporting requires submission by 8 AM. The batch has been creeping later due to portfolio growth and now finishes at 7:45 AM. The fix requires either algorithmic optimization, hardware scaling, or approximation methods. Decide the approach.
rubric_items: profile the batch process to identify the dominant runtime bottleneck
evaluate incremental VaR approximation against full recomputation accuracy requirements
assess horizontal scaling cost against the effort of algorithmic optimization
define an acceptable accuracy tolerance for any approximation method introduced
set a hard runtime target with automated alerting before the regulatory submission deadline

prompt: A self-driving car company's simulation suite covers 10 million scenarios, but a fatal edge case was found in production that none of the simulations captured. Adding adversarial scenario generation could prevent future gaps but slows simulation throughput by 40%. Decide how to integrate adversarial scenarios without falling behind on regression testing.
rubric_items: analyze the fatal edge case to identify the simulation coverage gap category
prioritize adversarial generation for scenario families with the highest real-world incidence
run adversarial generation as a separate lower-priority pipeline to protect regression throughput
define a minimum regression test throughput floor before adding adversarial workloads
track adversarial scenario coverage as a first-class metric alongside regression pass rate

prompt: A tech company's employee engagement survey reveals that the platform team has 40% lower satisfaction than other teams. The platform team maintains critical infrastructure and losing members would be catastrophic. The team lead attributes it to boring work; HR attributes it to management style. Design an investigation that identifies the real cause within 2 weeks.
rubric_items: collect anonymous structured data to test boring-work and management hypotheses independently
conduct stay and exit interviews within the first week of the investigation
compare platform team workload composition against benchmarks for similar engineering roles
use 360-degree feedback with a neutral facilitator to assess management behaviors
rank hypotheses by evidence strength before committing to any intervention

prompt: A distributed database cluster experiences a network partition during a multi-region deployment. Region A has the write master but stale replicas; Region B has up-to-date replicas but no write capability. Customer transactions are failing in both regions. Decide how to restore service while minimizing data loss.
rubric_items: measure the data freshness gap between Region A master and Region B replicas
promote a Region B replica to accept writes only if data loss is within the defined SLA
buffer and queue Region A writes for replay after the partition heals
communicate service degradation status to customers before restoring partial service
define a conflict resolution policy for transactions that diverged during the partition

prompt: A biotech startup has promising gene therapy results in mice but needs to decide between a Phase 1 human trial (18 months, $15M) and licensing the technology to a pharma company (immediate revenue but loss of control). The patent expires in 8 years. Frame the decision analysis.
rubric_items: estimate expected value for each path under optimistic and pessimistic trial scenarios
assess the licensing term length against the remaining patent exclusivity window
model Phase 1 success probability using the existing mouse efficacy data
evaluate whether licensing terms preserve re-acquisition rights if the licensee fails
identify hybrid deal structures that capture upfront revenue while retaining trial rights

prompt: An ad-tech company discovers that 20% of their attributed conversions are likely fraudulent click injections. Reporting this to advertisers would reduce revenue and trust. Not reporting it risks legal action if discovered later. The fraud detection system needs 6 weeks to reach production quality. Plan the disclosure and remediation timeline.
rubric_items: quantify legal exposure of delayed disclosure against the revenue cost of immediate notification
notify affected advertisers proactively before the fraud detection system reaches production
offer make-good credits to advertisers for verified fraudulent conversions
set a hard internal deadline for completing the fraud detection system
document the discovery timeline and remediation steps to demonstrate good-faith compliance

prompt: A warehouse automation system's path-planning algorithm occasionally creates deadlocks where 4 or more robots block each other. Each deadlock takes 3 minutes of manual intervention to resolve. The algorithm works perfectly for 3 or fewer robots in the same zone. Decide between zone capacity limits, deadlock detection and recovery, or a new planning algorithm.
rubric_items: measure deadlock frequency and zone occupancy distribution to scope the problem
evaluate zone capacity limits as an immediate low-risk mitigation
design a deadlock detection and recovery protocol with a bounded maximum resolution time
validate a new planning algorithm in simulation before any live deployment
define a phased rollout plan that limits blast radius while the permanent fix is proven

prompt: A space mission's flight software has a confirmed bug that causes a 0.1% chance of sensor data corruption per orbit. The satellite is already in orbit and can receive software updates, but each update attempt has a 2% chance of bricking the satellite. The mission has 3 years of planned operation remaining. Decide whether to patch.
rubric_items: calculate expected cumulative data corruption across the full 3-year remaining mission
compare expected mission loss from bricking against the cost of ongoing sensor corruption
assess whether a staged patch with rollback capability reduces the effective bricking probability
evaluate redundant sensor fusion as a mitigation that avoids patching entirely
consult flight software specialists for lower-risk patch delivery alternatives before deciding

prompt: A machine learning platform team needs to migrate from TensorFlow 1.x to PyTorch. There are 47 production models in TF1.x, and the team has 3 ML engineers. Converting each model takes roughly 1 week including validation. Meanwhile, new model development is blocked on the old framework. Plan the migration to minimize total business impact.
rubric_items: prioritize migration order by model business criticality and conversion complexity
unblock new model development on PyTorch immediately in parallel with migration work
define a validation gate confirming each migrated model matches TF1.x inference outputs
batch similar model architectures to reduce redundant conversion effort
set a total migration timeline that aligns with team capacity and acceptable business risk

prompt: A social media platform detects a coordinated inauthentic behavior campaign 48 hours before a national election. Removing the accounts would trigger accusations of censorship; leaving them up enables misinformation. The campaign uses a mix of real and fake accounts that are hard to separate. Decide the intervention strategy.
rubric_items: distinguish real accounts from fake accounts within the mixed campaign
address the censorship accusation risk of mass account removal
propose a graduated intervention that limits misinformation spread before the election
account for the 48-hour election timeline in the intervention sequencing
define escalation criteria for cross-functional and legal decision-making

prompt: A construction company's project management software shows that 3 out of 5 active projects are behind schedule. The shared crane and concrete crew are bottlenecks. Accelerating any one project by adding overtime delays another. Determine which project to prioritize and what the decision criteria should be.
rubric_items: identify decision criteria for prioritizing among the three delayed projects
address the shared crane and concrete crew as the core scheduling bottleneck
quantify the tradeoff between accelerating one project and delaying others
consider contractual penalties and delivery urgency in prioritization logic
propose a resource sequencing plan for crane and crew allocation across projects

prompt: A language model serving infrastructure handles 10K requests per second. A new safety filter must be applied to every response, adding 80ms of latency. Batching the filter improves throughput but increases p99 latency from 200ms to 600ms. Running the filter asynchronously risks serving unfiltered responses for a brief window. Choose an architecture.
rubric_items: evaluate the tradeoff between batching throughput gains and p99 latency increase to 600ms
address the unfiltered response safety risk of the asynchronous filter approach
define acceptable latency bounds relative to the current 200ms p99 baseline
consider a hybrid approach that batches low-risk request types separately
specify fallback behavior if the safety filter times out or becomes unavailable

prompt: A data team discovers that the warehouse ETL has been silently truncating decimal precision for 4 months, rounding financial figures to the nearest dollar instead of cent. Downstream dashboards and reports were used for strategic decisions during this period. Plan the data recovery, stakeholder communication, and prevention strategy.
rubric_items: identify which downstream strategic decisions used imprecise cent-truncated financial data
define a data recovery procedure to backfill cent-level precision from the source system
communicate the issue to stakeholders with clear scope and impact assessment
audit all reports and dashboards generated during the four-month precision loss window
add ETL validation checks to detect silent decimal truncation going forward

prompt: A drone delivery startup must choose between two coverage expansion strategies: adding 5 small depots across a metro area (lower per-depot cost, complex logistics) or 1 large central depot with longer-range drones (simpler logistics, higher per-delivery cost). Regulatory approval timelines differ for each approach. Design the decision analysis.
rubric_items: compare per-delivery cost and logistics complexity across the two depot strategies
account for regulatory approval timeline differences in the expansion decision
evaluate coverage quality versus per-depot infrastructure cost for each approach
define decision criteria that weigh operational complexity against long-range drone cost
incorporate market timing risk from the longer regulatory approval path into the analysis

prompt: A compiler team finds that their new optimization pass improves performance by 12% on benchmarks but introduces a miscompilation bug that affects 1 in 50,000 functions. The bug corrupts output silently. The optimization pass took 6 months to build. Decide whether to ship with a conservative heuristic, invest in formal verification, or shelve the pass.
rubric_items: quantify the silent miscompilation risk against the 12% benchmark performance benefit
evaluate whether a conservative heuristic can bound the class of affected functions
assess the feasibility and cost of formal verification relative to the optimization pass value
define a safe deployment gate such as an opt-in flag or restricted function scope
address the six-month sunk cost in terms of forward-looking risk rather than as justification to ship

prompt: An insurance company's pricing model uses 47 features, but a fairness audit reveals that 3 features are highly correlated with protected characteristics. Removing them drops pricing accuracy by 8%, leading to either higher premiums for all or increased loss ratios. Design an approach that maintains actuarial soundness while satisfying fairness requirements.
rubric_items: identify causal or proxy features that can replace the three protected-characteristic-correlated features
quantify the actuarial accuracy loss and its effect on premiums and loss ratios
address the tradeoff between pricing accuracy and discriminatory pricing liability
propose a fairness-constrained modeling approach such as adversarial debiasing or reweighting
engage legal and compliance stakeholders to define acceptable fairness thresholds before retraining

prompt: A multiplayer game's matchmaking algorithm optimizes for skill balance, but players complain about long queue times. Relaxing the skill threshold reduces wait times but creates lopsided matches that drive player churn. The game's concurrent population varies 5x between peak and off-peak. Design an adaptive matchmaking strategy.
rubric_items: adapt skill threshold dynamically based on current concurrent player population level
define separate matchmaking parameters for peak and off-peak population windows
quantify player churn impact of lopsided matches versus extended queue wait times
set a maximum queue time cap that triggers progressive skill threshold relaxation
monitor player retention metrics to validate threshold adjustment effects over time

prompt: A research hospital's imaging AI detects potential tumors with 95% sensitivity but only 70% specificity, generating many false positives that overwhelm radiologists with extra reads. Increasing the specificity threshold to 85% would miss 5% of real tumors. Decide how to deploy the system in a way that helps rather than hinders the radiology workflow.
rubric_items: define a detection threshold policy that balances missed tumor risk against radiologist overload
triage flagged cases by confidence score to prioritize the radiologist review queue
quantify the workflow capacity impact of the current 30% false positive rate
establish a feedback loop using radiologist adjudications to retrain and improve specificity
define clinical escalation criteria for low-confidence or borderline detections

prompt: A semiconductor fab discovers contamination in one of its cleanrooms. Production must halt for decontamination, but 3 customer orders are due in 10 days. Shifting production to another fab line is possible but requires requalification that takes 5 days. Some orders have contractual penalty clauses. Plan the production recovery.
rubric_items: assess whether the alternate fab line requalification can complete within the five-day window
prioritize orders by contractual penalty clause severity and delivery urgency
scope the decontamination timeline against the ten-day order deadline
negotiate partial delivery or schedule extensions with affected customers proactively
run fab line requalification in parallel with cleanroom decontamination to minimize recovery time

prompt: A school district is deploying AI-powered tutoring software. Teachers report it helps struggling students but bores advanced students, who disengage entirely. The vendor's adaptive difficulty feature is not working as advertised. The district paid for a full-year license. Decide whether to continue, supplement, or replace the software mid-year.
rubric_items: assess whether the vendor can fix the adaptive difficulty feature within a usable timeframe
segment deployment so advanced students have an alternative or supplementary engagement path
define measurable learning outcomes to evaluate software effectiveness through the remainder of the year
weigh the sunk license cost against ongoing harm from advanced student disengagement
identify supplementary materials that compensate for the broken adaptive difficulty feature

prompt: A payments company processes transactions in 23 currencies. A new anti-money-laundering rule requires real-time conversion to a base currency for threshold checking, but exchange rate APIs have 500ms latency and occasional failures. Using stale rates risks compliance violations; waiting for fresh rates risks transaction timeouts. Design the rate management strategy.
rubric_items: define a maximum acceptable rate staleness window that satisfies AML threshold compliance
implement a cached rate with a controlled refresh interval and a well-defined failure fallback
handle exchange rate API failure modes with a conservative worst-case rate or transaction hold
monitor drift between cached and live rates to trigger mandatory cache invalidation
distinguish high-risk transaction patterns that require fresh rates from low-risk routine ones

prompt: A machine learning team's model registry has 230 registered models, but only 40 are actively serving traffic. The remaining models have no documented owners and uncertain deprecation status. Deleting unused models saves storage and reduces confusion, but some may be needed for regulatory audit trails. Plan the cleanup.
rubric_items: identify which models have regulatory audit trail requirements before scheduling any deletion
contact last-known owners or teams to establish deprecation status for each unowned model
define retention criteria separating audit-required models from safely deletable inactive ones
archive rather than delete models with uncertain status pending ownership resolution
establish a model ownership policy to prevent undocumented registrations going forward

prompt: A city's emergency dispatch system routes ambulances using historical response time data. A new hospital opened 3 months ago, changing optimal routing, but the system hasn't been recalibrated. Updating the model requires 2 weeks of data collection from the new hospital. In the interim, some neighborhoods have suboptimal response times. Plan the transition.
rubric_items: apply interim manual routing overrides for neighborhoods with measurably degraded response times
begin the two-week data collection from the new hospital immediately without waiting for model updates
identify which specific neighborhoods are affected using historical response time data
define a parallel validation process before deploying the recalibrated routing model
set response time benchmarks to confirm recalibration has restored performance after deployment

prompt: A SaaS company's multi-tenant architecture shares a single database. One customer's analytics queries are causing lock contention that degrades performance for all tenants. Migrating that customer to a dedicated instance takes 2 weeks. Throttling their queries would violate their enterprise SLA. Design an immediate mitigation.
rubric_items: apply database resource governor limits or query isolation without triggering SLA throttling
schedule the offending analytics workload during off-peak hours to reduce lock contention
evaluate read replicas or query routing to absorb analytics load away from the primary write path
accelerate the dedicated instance migration by parallelizing provisioning and testing steps
communicate proactively with the enterprise customer about the mitigation plan and timeline

prompt: A deepfake detection system deployed by a news organization flags 12% of legitimate videos as manipulated. Lowering sensitivity lets actual deepfakes through. Publishing a retraction for a falsely flagged video damages credibility. Not catching a real deepfake damages credibility more. Design the editorial workflow around the detector's limitations.
rubric_items: require human review for all detector-flagged videos before publication
define confidence tiers that route high-confidence detections differently from borderline ones
establish a publication hold policy for flagged content pending secondary editorial review
maintain an audit log of detector decisions and human override outcomes for accountability
document the 12% false positive rate in internal editorial guidelines to calibrate reviewer expectations

prompt: A manufacturing plant's predictive maintenance model correctly predicted 3 out of 4 recent equipment failures but also generated 15 false alarms. Each false alarm costs $8K in unnecessary downtime for inspection. Each missed failure costs $200K in unplanned downtime. Determine the optimal alert threshold and maintenance scheduling policy.
rubric_items: calculate expected total cost at multiple thresholds using the $8K false alarm and $200K miss cost asymmetry
set the alert threshold to minimize expected downtime cost rather than maximize raw detection rate
define a risk-stratified inspection protocol that reduces false alarm response cost
incorporate equipment age and usage hours as features to improve alert precision over time
track false alarm rate alongside miss rate to validate threshold adjustment decisions

prompt: A language model API provider wants to add usage-based pricing but has customers on flat-rate plans who would see 3x cost increases. Grandfathering old plans indefinitely loses revenue; forcing migration risks churn. The top 5% of users consume 60% of compute. Design a pricing transition that retains customers while improving unit economics.
rubric_items: grandfather existing flat-rate customers for a defined transition period with advance notice
target usage-based migration at the top five percent of users who consume sixty percent of compute
model projected churn against revenue gain to set a grandfathering expiration timeline
design tiered pricing that improves heavy-user unit economics while protecting moderate users
offer migration incentives such as credits or locked rates to reduce flat-rate customer resistance

prompt: A satellite constellation operator discovers that two satellites in adjacent orbital planes have a projected close approach in 96 hours. Maneuvering either satellite uses propellant that reduces mission lifetime by 2 months. Not maneuvering has a 1-in-10,000 collision probability. Decide the maneuver criteria and timing.
rubric_items: compare the 1-in-10,000 collision probability against the 2-month mission lifetime cost of maneuvering
define a probability threshold that triggers mandatory maneuver without further deliberation
determine optimal maneuver timing within the 96-hour window to minimize propellant expenditure
verify the collision probability estimate with independent tracking data before finalizing the decision
evaluate which satellite maneuver minimizes total mission impact across both objects

prompt: A cross-functional team must deliver an MVP in 8 weeks. The designer wants a polished UI, the backend engineer wants a robust API, and the data scientist wants a well-validated model. Doing all three properly would take 14 weeks. Decide what to cut, what to defer, and what quality bar each component must meet for a credible demo.
rubric_items: define minimum viable quality bars for UI, API, and model that each support a credible demo
identify which components or features can be deferred post-MVP without breaking the demo path
align the cross-functional team on a single prioritized scope before development begins
cut non-essential features rather than reducing depth on the core demo-critical components
specify a post-MVP roadmap that commits deferred items to a concrete follow-up timeline

prompt: A bank's fraud detection model was trained on data from before a pandemic-era shift in spending patterns. Post-pandemic, normal transactions look anomalous and fraud patterns changed. Retraining on recent data alone loses pre-pandemic fraud signatures. Using all data dilutes recent patterns. Design the retraining strategy.
rubric_items: use time-weighted training that emphasizes recent data without discarding pre-pandemic fraud signatures
segment training data by temporal period and evaluate each period's contribution independently
evaluate an ensemble blending a pre-pandemic model with a recent-data model for combined coverage
recalibrate decision thresholds on recent labeled transactions before committing to full retraining
define evaluation benchmarks that test for both pre-pandemic fraud signatures and post-pandemic spending patterns

prompt: An autonomous mining operation's fleet management system optimizes for ore throughput, but operators report it creates dangerous traffic patterns at intersections. Slowing vehicles at intersections reduces throughput by 15%. Adding more intersection infrastructure costs $2M and takes 6 months. Design an interim safety solution.
rubric_items: implement intersection traffic control rules within the fleet management system as an immediate interim fix
quantify the throughput reduction from intersection slowdowns against the safety risk being mitigated
define a safety incident threshold that mandates operational halts before committing to the $2M infrastructure investment
audit intersection sensor and traffic logs to identify the highest-risk patterns and locations immediately
evaluate lower-cost interim measures such as physical barriers or signaling as an alternative to full infrastructure spend

prompt: A security team discovers a zero-day vulnerability in a library used by 80% of the company's microservices. Patching all services simultaneously is impossible due to testing requirements. Prioritizing by exposure creates a 2-week window where unpatched services are known-vulnerable. An attacker is actively scanning for the vulnerability. Plan the patching sequence and interim protections.
rubric_items: prioritize patching sequence by external exposure ranking the most internet-facing services first
deploy network-level mitigations such as WAF rules or firewall blocks to reduce attack surface during the patch window
establish monitoring and alerting for active exploitation attempts against the vulnerable library during patching
define the patching sequence and testing cadence to maximize speed without skipping critical validation
isolate or temporarily take offline the highest-risk unpatched services that cannot be addressed in the first wave

prompt: A research lab's compute cluster is shared between training runs and interactive notebook users. Training jobs are long-running and preemptible; notebook users need immediate GPU access for debugging. The cluster is at 95% utilization. Adding a priority queue for notebooks would preempt training jobs, extending their completion time. Removing notebook access would slow research iteration. Design a resource allocation policy that balances both needs.
rubric_items: define a time-bounded GPU reservation for notebook debugging sessions to limit training job preemption
set minimum guaranteed training job slots that notebook priority requests cannot preempt below
implement a notebook request queue with a maximum acceptable wait time before granting preemptible capacity
monitor cluster utilization to detect when notebook preemption materially extends training job completion times
explore per-job checkpointing to reduce the cost and disruption of preempting long-running training jobs
